advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Measure `fold_s` over only the locked fold (exclude the post-lock push) so the `_SHORTEST_PASS_S` decision reflects lock-hold time as its comment claims.
evidence: `_sweep_one_ticket` now calls `push.push_after_commit(tracker)` after the fold released the lock (compact.py:367-373), so that push time is included in `fold_s`

lock.py:313-315 defines `_SHORTEST_PASS_S` as 'the shortest pass any acquire() caller can ask for ... A fold shorter than this cannot have outlasted a waiter's pass' — i.e. the threshold is about lock-held time, not wall time of the whole ticket
advisory.finding: `fold_s` measures the whole `_sweep_one_ticket` call, which now includes the post-lock `push.push_after_commit(tracker)`, but `_give_waiters_a_turn` uses `fold_s >= _SHORTEST_PASS_S` to decide whether a waiter could be in retry backoff — a judgement about how long the LOCK was held. A slow push inflates `fold_s` past 1.0s even when the locked section was brief, so the sweep pays the longer (backoff-cap) pause when no waiter can be in backoff.
scenarios: A fold whose locked section is <1s but whose per-fold push to origin is slow (network latency) pushes fold_s over _SHORTEST_PASS_S.
advisory.suggested_fix: Time only the fold/lock portion — e.g. have `_sweep_one_ticket` return the locked-section duration, or capture `time.monotonic()` immediately after the `compact_cli` fold and before the push — and base `_give_waiters_a_turn` on that.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that fails a per-fold `push_after_commit` and asserts the sweep still completes all folds and the end-of-run safety-net push delivers the pending fold to origin.
evidence: compact.py:367-373 adds the per-fold push: `if not no_commit: ... push.push_after_commit(tracker)` with the comment 'a failed push stays pending for the end-of-run push.'
push.py:515-529 shows push_after_commit swallows non-strict Exception (PUSH_PENDING) but re-raises OptionalDependencyError — so a failing per-fold push has two distinct outcomes, neither tested.

advisory.finding: No test covers the new per-fold-push failure/safety-net contract the diff introduces: a per-fold `push.push_after_commit` that fails must leave the sweep running with the fold pending for the end-of-run safety-net push. All added tests exercise only the success path (each fold reaches origin) or the no-commit path (never pushes); none injects a failing per-fold push to confirm the sweep continues and the end-of-run push recovers the undelivered fold.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch push.push_after_commit to raise on the first fold only, run compact_all_cli against store_with_origin, and assert (a) the sweep folds all tickets (does not abort) and (b) _unpushed(repo) == 0 after the end-of-run push — proving the safety net recovered the failed per-fold push.
